title: Gapped text: The Hungry Caterpillar Problem

passages.title: The Hungry Caterpillar Problem
passages.intro: 5 sentences have been removed. Choose the sentence that best fits each gap. There is one extra sentence you do not need.
passages.credit: Original text written for this practice.
paragraphs: When Ms Patel's class set up a vegetable garden, they planted lettuce, beans and cabbages. Everything grew well for a few weeks. [[1]]
The students looked closely and found small green caterpillars hiding under the leaves. [[2]] Soon the cabbages looked like lace.
Some students wanted to spray the plants with poison. Ms Patel said no. [[3]] Instead, the class decided to find a natural way to protect the garden.
They read that some birds love to eat caterpillars. [[4]] Within a week, wrens and willie wagtails were visiting the garden every morning.
The caterpillars did not disappear completely, but there were far fewer of them. [[5]] The class has decided to keep the bird bath full all year round.

bank.A: Poison could harm the bees, worms and birds that help the garden.
bank.B: So they built a bird bath and planted small bushes where birds could shelter.
bank.C: Then, one morning, the cabbage leaves were full of holes.
bank.D: They were munching holes in the cabbage leaves.
bank.F: The cabbages grew back, and the class picked them at the end of term.
